messages.subject: jitter in layer() syntax
parts:
What do the "width" and "height" attributes of jitter really do? The example below seems to demonstrate that setting these attributes to zero does *not* remove the jitter.

The two tasks attempted in this post are

(1) to make the simplest of dotplots, i.e., for a single continuous variable, and

(2) to jitter this plot so that repeated identical values are visible.

We need jitter in the meaningless (y) direction but not in the x direction. I thought that the width and height arguments would do this, but the example below seems to show otherwise.

I use the layer() syntax because that forces me to think carefully about the components of the grammar. The shortcuts (geom_jitter, qplot, etc) seem to mask what is going on.

set.seed(1)
# Sort to make it easier to see what we have
DAAT <- data.frame( X=sort(exp(sample(rnorm(20), replace=T))), zero=0)
print(DAAT)
layer2<-layer(
data=DAAT
, mapping=aes(x=X, y=zero)
, geom="point"
, geom_params=list(shape=1)
, jitter_params=list(height=9, width=0)
, position="jitter"
)
print(
ggplot() + layer2
+ scale_y_continuous(name="", expand=c(0,1), breaks=0, labels="")
)
# "expand" seems to control the amount of vertical space around the points.
# Incidentally, how would I get rid of the tick on the y axis?

# If we set both jitter parameters to zero, there should be no jitter at all.
layer2<-layer(
data=DAAT
, mapping=aes(x=X, y=zero)
, geom="point"
, geom_params=list(shape=1)
, jitter_params=list(height=0, width=0)
, position="jitter"
)
print(
ggplot() + layer2
+ scale_y_continuous(name="", expand=c(0,1), breaks=0, labels="")
)
# But there is lots of jitter!

# Although the shortcut position_jitter() is documented, I have found no
# documentation for the full general syntax that uses layer() and position=jitter.

What is going on? How do I make the jitter in one or both directions zero?

An alternate way would be to explicitly create a jittered y variable, but that seems to contradict the notion that we can explicitly specify a "jitter" component of our grammar of graphics:

DAAT$geetar<-scale(runif(nrow(DAAT)))/3
layer3<-layer(
data=DAAT
, mapping=aes(x=X, y=geetar)
, geom="point"
, geom_params=list(shape=1)
)
print(
ggplot() + layer3
+ scale_y_continuous(name="", expand=c(0,1), breaks=0, labels="")
)

On Apr 15, 6:02 pm, Jacob Wegelin <jacobwege...@fastmail.fm> wrote:
> What do the "width" and "height" attributes of jitter really do? The example below seems to demonstrate that setting these attributes to zero does *not* remove the jitter.

> print(
>         ggplot() + layer2
>         + scale_y_continuous(name="", expand=c(0,1), breaks=0, labels="")
>         )
> #       "expand" seems to control the amount of vertical space around the points.
> #       Incidentally, how would I get rid of the tick on the y axis?

Setting breaks=NA should get rid of all of the y-axis display,
including labels, tick marks, and lines:

>
> #       If we set both jitter parameters to zero, there should be no jitter at all.
> layer2<-layer(
>         data=DAAT
>         , mapping=aes(x=X, y=zero)
>         , geom="point"
>         , geom_params=list(shape=1)
>         , jitter_params=list(height=0, width=0)
>         , position="jitter"
>         )
> print(
>         ggplot() + layer2
>         + scale_y_continuous(name="", expand=c(0,1), breaks=0, labels="")
>         )
> #       But there is lots of jitter!
>
> #       Although the shortcut position_jitter() is documented, I have found no
> #       documentation for the full general syntax that uses layer() and position=jitter.
>
> What is going on? How do I make the jitter in one or both directions zero?

I'm not familiar with the syntax you are using (in particular, I don't
think "jitter_params" does anything). One way to write it would be:

, position=position_jitter(width=0, height=0)
)


I agree with you that qplot, whlle an easy-to-use interface to get
started, is somewhat confusing once you are doing more complicated
things. I wouldn't use qplot in this case, but rather the full
ggplot() syntax to build up a layer manually. If I were writing your
first example, I would probably do it something like this:

# "zero" column not necessary, just set aesthetic to 0 in the mapping!
DAAT <- data.frame( X=sort(exp(sample(rnorm(20), replace=T))))
# Use ggplot() call to set up data source and aesthetic mapping
ggplot(data=DAAT, mapping=aes(x=X, y=0)) +
# Create a point layer using geom_point, and set position to
position_jitter with desired parameters
geom_point(shape=I(1), position=position_jitter(width=0, height=9)) +
# Remove y-axis display by setting breaks=NA
scale_y_continuous(name="", breaks=NA)

Hope this is helpful!

Josh.
